topic: Per-page JS/CSS weight: ticket says every page loads data it doesn't need
context: Rails app at <REPO> (importmap, Stimulus, Turbo). Prod <PROD_URL>. Lead has established: /assets served no-store; eager controller loading pulls every library on every page.
rules: Prod: only unauthenticated GETs of the public login page and its assets, at most 8 page loads per stream.

streams.prompt: Cold x3 and warm reload x2 of the login page: every request with origin, size, cache-control, served-from-cache. Break totals down by source, top 10 by bytes. Save HAR.
CDP profiler and trace, 3 runs unthrottled and 3 at 4x CPU: script time per URL, long tasks, DCL/load. Say if per-URL attribution is unreliable.
Static analysis: for each heavy library, which modules import it, which controllers use it, which views mount them. Dead controllers. Globals that break under lazy loading.
Why is /assets no-store? git log -S and PR history, any pentest findings, current headers via curl -I, and what RFC 9111, RFC 8246 and OWASP say. What must stay no-store?
Risk of lazy controller loading, moving imports out of application.js, on-demand loaders and far-future caching, including old-browser shims. Rate benefit, risk and how to verify each.
How often do users pay the full-load cost? Code paths that bypass Turbo, plus any read-only telemetry (logs, RUM). Mark estimates as inferred.
